Rep. Jason Zachary highlights youth activism, election day reminder, and Marsha Blackburn's AI bill
Rep. Jason Zachary, a member of the Tennessee House of Representatives, used his social media platform to comment on recent political and legislative developments in early August 2026.
On August 4, Zachary expressed support for young women speaking out publicly by posting, "Proud of these young ladies who are boldly and tactfully speaking truth."
The following day, he encouraged voter participation in upcoming elections. On August 5, he posted, "Tomorrow is Election Day! Please make plans to vote for your GOP candidates up and down the ballot. #VoteGOP"
Later that same day, Zachary highlighted legislative progress made by Marsha Blackburn, U.S. Senator from Tennessee and gubernatorial candidate at the time. He wrote, ".@VoteMarsha is in DC today and just passed her bill out of committee to protect children when using AI. BIG WIN! We forget that she is still leading in DC, passing her own bills, and standing for TN while running for Governor. Not rhetoric from Marsha. She is the leader we".
Blackburn’s work on legislation related to child safety and artificial intelligence aligns with broader national discussions about regulating AI technology to protect minors online—a topic that has gained attention as policymakers seek new safeguards amid rapid technological change.
Tennessee’s primary elections typically occur in August during even-numbered years. Voter turnout efforts often intensify in the days leading up to Election Day as candidates and their supporters mobilize constituents across the state.
